author: jlindner
title: UPDATE: Gun found at Campbell Middle School, student arrested - NewsBreak
text:
By jlindner ,
12 hours ago The Cobb County School District’s headquarters is at 514 Glover St. in Marietta. By Special A Campbell Middle School student is in custody after a gun was found in their possession at the school Tuesday, school officials announced.
A spokesperson from the Cobb School District confirmed to the Journal that a Campbell student was discovered in possession of a firearm after a separate student told an administrator.
A letter from Campbell Principal LaEla Mitchell sent to the school community Tuesday confirmed that a firearm was confiscated from the unidentified suspected student, but didn’t specify what kind.
According to Mitchell, the firearm was “not used in any threat against students, staff or the campus.” However, the district’s investigation has since learned that may not have been the case.
“We don’t know for a fact that there was not a threat made. I don’t know specifically what kind of threats were made or what was said, but that is why that letter says there was no threat made,” the spokesperson told the Journal. “With any investigation, things change, and we had initial information that did not indicate that there was a threat made.”
School and district officials did not confirm whether the district’s Vapor Wake K-9s were on scene when the gun was discovered.
However, thanks to “multiple layers of safety supports, including students and staff who did as they were trained,” officials were able to respond immediately to the scene, secure the situation and take the student into custody.
After the weapon was confiscated, the school day continued without disruption, Mitchell reports.
“Moments like this are exactly why we invest significant time and resources in multiple layers of security; the processes worked as designed and kept our campus secure,” Mitchell said. “We’re thankful for the district’s ongoing commitment to safety and for the training our team receives. Our team was ready and kept the children safe.”
The suspected student has been charged in connection with the incident, according to the district, and will “now face the full range of legal consequences,” per Mitchell’s letter.
The district has not specified what the suspect has been charged with.
The incident comes just a week-and-a-half into the start of the 2026-2027 school year.
“The Cobb County School District Police Department continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident, work with other law enforcement agencies, and we are grateful that the safety protocols at Campbell Middle worked,” the spokesperson said.
Cobb Board of Education member Becky Sayler, who represents the school, said she was grateful for the outcome of the situation.
“I’m just very relieved that (it) was the best possible outcome for a very sad and scary situation,” Sayler said. “I’m very grateful to all the adults that did the right thing in that situation.”
